title: Adversarial Machine Learning for Social Good: Reframing the Adversary as an Ally

bias_targets.methodology: The paper surveys existing literature that utilizes adversarial machine learning to mitigate gender bias, specifically reviewing methods like adversarial domain adaptation (FAIRDA) and adversarial glasses attacks to enhance fairness in classification and gender recognition models.

The paper reviews literature that applies adversarial domain adaptation modules to estimate and debias sensitive attributes such as race, transferring knowledge from a source domain to train a fair model in a target domain.

The paper summarizes approaches that use Projected Gradient Descent (PGD) attack algorithms to generate adversarial examples near the decision boundary, guiding the training of deep neural networks to alleviate the negative effects of class imbalance.

The paper reviews methods utilizing adversarial training on the client side of Federated Learning frameworks to enforce individual fairness by generating and training on examples that violate established similarity metrics.
